Hi Samantha — thanks, happy to put a concise MAP together. Draft below (attachments: Pioneer_MAP_v2.xlsx). High-level answers up front:

- Typical sequencing we recommend: 1) DPA review in parallel with evaluation, 2) MSA negotiation and redlines, 3) Order Form (signed) + PO issuance, 4) Final MSA signature (if customer requires signature on master only).
- In most enterprise cases Pioneer can issue a PO referencing the Order Form while MSA redlines are finalized, provided the Order Form contains the key commercial terms and a signature block. If Pioneer requires the fully executed MSA before PO, we can prioritize an expedited redline cycle.

Draft MAP (high-level):
- Week 0 (Mar 2–6): Exchange DPA draft and baseline MSA redlines. (Owner: Pioneer legal / Redwood legal)
- Week 1 (Mar 9–13): Redwood reviews and returns redlines; commercial team confirms order form values. (Owner: Redwood — Priya/Marcus)
- Week 2 (Mar 16–20): Legal sync call to resolve open redlines; finalize Order Form. (Owner: both counsels)
- Week 3 (Mar 23–27): Pioneer issues PO referencing Order Form; parties exchange signatures (Order Form via DocuSign). Target: provisioning window starts week of Mar 30. (Owner: Pioneer procurement / Redwood ops)
- Contingency: If MSA signature is required pre-PO, accelerate Week 2 to prioritize legal hours; target MSA exec by Mar 20.

Action items for Pioneer evaluation:
- Confirm whether PO can be issued referencing a signed Order Form while MSA follows, or if legal requires MSA before PO. (Owner: Pioneer — Samantha/Trevor)
- Send any Pioneer standard procurement terms that must be included in Order Form (PO language). (Owner: Pioneer)

I've attached a formal MAP spreadsheet (Pioneer_MAP_v2.xlsx) with date cells and owners. Priya / Marcus — please confirm on legal timing and whether the MSA redline schedule above is realistic.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attached are Pioneer legal's initial redlines to the MSA (MSA_redlines_RStern_20260303.pdf). Key items we flagged:
- Data processing scope (DPA) needs stronger controller/processor obligations and breach notification timelines.
- Liability cap: Pioneer requests a higher cap for regulated workloads.
- Termination for convenience: Pioneer prefers 30 days notice; Redwood default is 60.

We can take a prioritized approach: if Redwood can accept the DPA language and a limited set of commercial concessions, Pioneer procurement can move to issue a PO referencing the Order Form. If the liability cap remains an open item, Pioneer may require MSA signature first.

Please let us know which redlines Redwood will accept in principle so we can indicate to procurement what will be resolved pre-PO vs post-PO.
